locate.title: Find them
locate.summary: How to use the public government detainee locator, step by step.
locate.body: The public locator is a government website open to everyone. Enter the A-Number as 9 digits, with no dashes and no letter prefix, and select the country of birth. If the name was written differently on older documents, try that spelling too — names transliterated from another alphabet are often recorded in more than one way. Sometimes the locator returns a message asking you to call the agency for details, or returns nothing at all; this happens and does not by itself confirm where a person is.

money_calls.title: Money and calls
money_calls.summary: Setting up a phone account at the facility.
money_calls.body: Facilities use outside vendors for phone accounts. There are two account types: one funds the detained person's own calling balance, and another is tied to a specific family phone number. Families commonly confuse the two. Your facility's page in this app lists which vendor it uses and what each account funds.

mail_format.title: Mail format
mail_format.summary: How to address envelopes so mail reaches them.
mail_format.body: Facilities commonly require the full committed name and the A-Number on the envelope. Check your facility's page for its exact format before sending anything.

attorney_verification.title: Check an attorney's license
attorney_verification.summary: How families verify a license using public records.
attorney_verification.body: Every state bar keeps a free public search where you can look up a lawyer's license status and history. A federal list also names practitioners disciplined in immigration practice. Immigration court generally accepts attorneys licensed in any state; filings in federal district court generally require admission to that district. This is general information, not a judgment about any specific attorney.

start_documents.title: Start gathering documents
start_documents.summary: Documents proving years of residence are among the first things attorneys request.
start_documents.body: Families in this situation commonly gather documents year by year: tax records, leases, school records, medical records, bank statements, pay stubs, IDs, and photos. The Document Builder helps you organize what an attorney may ask for.

support_letters.title: Support letters
support_letters.summary: Keep track of letters from people who know your family.
support_letters.body: Attorneys sometimes ask families to collect letters from employers, teachers, neighbors, or faith communities. This app only tracks who you asked and whether the letter arrived — your attorney guides the content.

children_care.title: Children's care documentation
children_care.summary: Organize caregiver contacts, school info, and key documents.
children_care.body: Record who is caring for the children now, backup caregivers, school contacts, and store documents like birth certificates and insurance cards. For court-related questions, each state court system publishes official self-help resources — we link to them and give no other guidance.

send_securely.title: How to send documents securely
send_securely.summary: Share documents through private links, not email or messengers.
send_securely.body: Attorneys commonly ask clients not to send documents by email, text, or messenger. Use this app's expiring share link, or upload your packet to the portal your attorney gives you.
